_comment: The people the board schedules. Data, not code: add a row to add someone,
set active to false to take them off the board without deleting the
history that references them.
WHAT IS REAL HERE. Names are the lab roster from the shared Outlook
calendar. 'van_trained' is the manual's Van-Trained Staff list (Makenzie/Morgan,
Lauren, Ramiro, Emma, Maggie -- Emma is not a coordinator). 'manual_name'
is how the manual refers to them, which is what the reliability chart and
the all-day absence banners are keyed on.
WHAT IS SYNTHETIC. capacity_hours_week, completed_visits, zone, attributes,
in_lab_day, out_of_hours_count and committed_hours are invented to exercise
the engine and describe nobody's actual workload. Replace them from the
lab's own records before the pilot.
Clinical reliability is NOT here. It lives in reliability-matrix.json,
transcribed from the manual's chart, and that file alone decides who may
run a visit. Two places to say the same thing is how they end up
disagreeing.
'can_tech' says someone can run the tech side of a visit. The manual does
not publish a tech certification list, so everyone active carries it until

'credentials' are practical requirements for getting a visit done -- consent-taking, driving, kit handling. They are NOT clinical reliability, which lives in reliability-matrix.json. Everyone active holds CONSENT and DRIVING; the rest are synthetic until the lab records them.
the lab says otherwise; set it false to exclude somebody.
ROLES AND WHAT THEY ALLOW. 'roles' is what the board asks about a person,
never their name. coordinator schedules and has an in-lab day; clinician
can be THE clinician on a visit; tech can be the tech; grad_student goes
on visits on their own calendar's time and the manual says to check with
them before offering one, so the board flags that rather than assuming.
solo_from / solo_to are the manual's 'Visits Can Do Solo' column, which
is REAL and transcribed: Lauren and Sanjana 1m-12m, Makenzie 6m-12m.
Maggie, Ramiro and Sofia have no range printed beside their name,
so they cannot be the clinician however many assessments they are signed
off on. Being reliable in one assessment is not being able to run a visit.
only_checkpoints overrides the range for a row like Emma's, which reads
'*only schedule for 36m visits*'. She is not a coordinator so she is not
in this file; the field exists for when somebody like her is.
TO ADD A GRADUATE STUDENT: copy any row, give them roles
["grad_student", "tech"], set confirm_before_offering true, and leave
solo_from/solo_to unset unless they can run a visit alone. Nothing else
changes; no code knows their name.
MERGED AND INACTIVE RECORDS:
C05 is ONE person with two names. The Outlook export prints them
'Soto, Morgan'; the manual's reliability chart and the lab's
all-day absence banners call them 'Makenzie'. There was a
separate C07 'Makenzie' row, which was the same human recorded
twice, so it is merged into C05 rather than deactivated: the
printed name stays in 'name' so the export matches, the manual's
name is in 'manual_name' so the chart and banners match, and the
competencies are the manual-derived ones (clinician+tech, solo
6m-12m, van-trained, EEG).
STILL TO CONFIRM: capacity_hours_week. The two records disagreed
(10 vs 20) and neither number came from the manual. It is set to
20 because somebody running solo 6m-12m visits is unlikely to be
half-time, but that is an inference, not a transcription.
C06 Ramiro is active: false -- a real person the lab is not currently
scheduling. His calendar is still recognised as his, so the print
is fully explained and nobody is sent looking for a mapping that
is not missing. His blocks are not read: busy time for somebody
who can never be offered is time the board would never use.
